India ranked 131st among 145 countries in the index, and its position remained unchanged from the previous edition. Global Gender Gap Index The Global Gender Gap Index is an annual index published by the World Economic Forum . It measures gender parity across four dimensions: Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. India’s 2026 Position India recorded an overall gender parity score of 64.5% in 2026. This score was below the global average of 69.2%, which represented 69.2% of the gender gap closed worldwide. India’s rank of 131st was unchanged from the 2025 edition. The country’s overall score improved slightly in 2026, but the rank did not change. Key Dimensions in India’s Score Educational Attainment was India’s strongest dimension in 2026, with a parity score of 96.6%. Political Empowerment was India’s highest-ranked subindex, with 24.5% gender equality and a global rank of 67th. Economic Participation and Opportunity remained India’s weakest dimension in 2026, with 41.2% parity. Health and Survival is one of the four standard pillars used in the index. bihar_raw_news.title: BJP National President Nitin Nabin Donates Three Months' Salary to Bihar Flood Relief Fund
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 18, 2026 4:35 PM BJP National President Nitin Nabin Donates Three Months’ Salary to Bihar Flood Relief Fund Uttar Dinajpur: BJP National President Nitin Nabin addresses a public meeting ahead of the West Bengal Assembly election in Uttar Dinajpur district on Thursday, April 09, 2026. (Photo: IANS/X/@NitinNabin) Rajya Sabha MP and BJP National President Nitin Nabin contributed 6 lakh 35 thousand rupees from his three-month salary to the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund for Bihar floods. In a social media post, Mr Nabin said, “The government is continuously monitoring the flood situation in Bihar and is working with full preparedness to ensure timely relief and necessary assistance reaches the affected people.” He added that teams from the National Disaster Response Force and the State Disaster Response Force are deployed for rescue operations, along with arrangements for relief camps, community kitchens, medical facilities, and animal fodder. The MP further added that the process of assessing crop damage to farmers and providing necessary assistance is also underway. Mr Nabin informed us that the state government has provided a total amount exceeding 550 crore rupees as financial assistance of 7000 rupees per family to families affected by the floods.

bihar_raw_news.title: Vishnupad Temple Area to Get Rs 2,520 Crore Revamp Under Bihar's Gaya Tourism Push
bihar_raw_news.content: Industry Watch Articles News Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp The Bihar Cabinet has approved a ₹2,520-crore project for the comprehensive development of the Vishnupad Temple area in Gaya, as part of a wider infrastructure push aimed at strengthening the city’s religious tourism ecosystem. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on September 15. The Vishnupad development project will be undertaken on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi and will focus on improving infrastructure and visitor facilities around the temple. The proposed development includes redevelopment of the temple premises, multi-level car parking, an elevated pathway, the Manasarovar-Manpur Bridge, ramps, ghats, dormitories, a canteen and a pedestrian bridge. Public amenities and other associated infrastructure are also part of the project. Bihar Rajya Path Vikas Nigam Ltd. will implement the development. The Vishnupad Temple is an important pilgrimage destination in Gaya and attracts domestic and international visitors, particularly during the Pitru Paksha period, when devotees travel to the city for Pind Daan rituals. The Bihar Tourism Department has described the temple as significant from historical, traditional and religious perspectives. The infrastructure investment is expected to have an impact beyond the temple precinct, with improved visitor facilities and mobility potentially supporting Gaya’s wider tourism ecosystem. Accommodation, local transport, tour operations, food services and other visitor-oriented businesses form part of the wider pilgrimage economy. The ₹2,520-crore Vishnupad project was among a set of major infrastructure decisions approved by the Bihar Cabinet during the September 15 meeting. The Cabinet also approved ₹996.05 crore for the Son-Falgu River Linking Project, which includes the construction of an intake well approximately 23 kilometres upstream of the Indrapuri Barrage and an approximately 11-kilometre pipeline to the Uttar Koyal Main Canal. The Cabinet further approved a memorandum of understanding between the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India and the Bihar government to expand regional air connectivity under the Centre’s Modified UDAN scheme. The arrangement is intended to support new air routes and provide assistance for routes with lower passenger demand during their initial operating period. Together, the infrastructure and connectivity measures signal a broader focus on improving the visitor infrastructure around Gaya, with the Vishnupad Temple area emerging as a key component of Bihar’s religious and cultural tourism development plans.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Agri dept to provide free sugarcane seeds to farmers under expansion scheme
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Muzaffarpur: The Bihar Agriculture Department will provide free sugarcane seed to farmers to encourage expansion of sugarcane cultivation across the state. Under the Sugarcane Expansion Scheme, farmers will be supported for cultivation across 200 acres, with applications to be submitted online, Jagran reported. Farmers cultivating up to one hectare will be eligible to receive the seed free of cost. The initiative is aimed at increasing the area under sugarcane cultivation and improving farm incomes. Assistant Sugarcane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said a special campaign would be conducted across all 16 blocks of Muzaffarpur district to promote sugarcane planting. Farmers from each block can apply online to avail themselves of the scheme. The government will also provide subsidies to farmers for purchasing fertilizers and pesticides as part of the initiative. The department plans to promote sugarcane cultivation through greater access to quality planting material and cultivation support. Ravi said farmers could adopt two methods of sugarcane cultivation. In the first method, cane stalks are cut and planted directly in the field, requiring around 25 quintals of seed per acre. The second method involves planting nursery-raised seedlings, with around 10,000 plants required per acre. Sugarcane planting is generally undertaken in October and February. Once the crop is established from the initial planting material, farmers can obtain two additional crops through ratooning with the application of fertilizers and other inputs, according to the department. Under the scheme, farmers will be able to obtain planting material from designated nurseries. The department will directly pay the cost of the seed to the nursery operators. Ravi said sugarcane cultivation could provide significant returns to farmers. According to the department, an acre can produce around 300–400 quintals of sugarcane, potentially generating a profit of around ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh after cultivation costs. The department said it would continue implementing schemes to promote sugarcane cultivation and support higher farm incomes in Bihar.

bihar_raw_news.content: News Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet. Manish Kumar 18 Sep 2026 09:48 IST Follow Us Bihar Floats Solar Dryer Plan, Seeks OEMs for Farm-Level Deployments Photograph: (AI) The Bihar Horticulture Development Society has invited bids from OEMs and authorised agencies for the supply, installation and maintenance of solar crop dryers across multiple capacity categories, ranging from 20 kg to 1,000 kg per batch. Advertisment The Bihar Horticulture Development Society (BHDS), under the state’s Department of Agriculture, has floated a request for proposal (RFP) to empanel Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and OEM-authorised agencies for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, warranty support and maintenance of solar crop dryers across Bihar. Advertisment The procurement covers solar crop dryers with capacities of 20/25 kg, 50 kg, 100 kg, 250 kg, 500 kg and a special 1,000-kg category, according to the RFP. The dryers are intended to support farmers and horticulture-related users in drying agricultural and horticultural produce. The tender has been floated through the Bihar government's e-procurement portal. The last date for submission of bids is October 8, 2026, at 3 pm, while technical bids are scheduled to open the same day at 3:30 pm. A pre-bid meeting is scheduled for September 24 at 1:15 pm in hybrid/online mode. The date for financial bid opening will be communicated to technically qualified bidders. Advertisment Six capacity categories The RFP has divided the solar crop dryers into different capacity packages based on their intended users. The smallest 20/25-kg package is aimed at individual farmers, kitchen gardens and small medicinal or aromatic plant growers, with portable cabinet, box or foldable configurations envisaged. The 50-kg category is intended for progressive farmers, small self-help groups (SHGs), nurseries and demonstration centres, while the 100-kg category targets SHGs, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), village enterprises and common facility centres. Advertisment The larger 250-kg package is designed for FPOs, farmer clusters and institutional buyers, while the 500-kg category targets large FPOs, aggregation centres and processing clusters. A special 1,000-kg category is reserved for cluster or institutional projects and can be deployed only after site feasibility, civil-space confirmation, power/backup planning and separate approval by BHDS. Advertisment Solar-powered drying system The tender defines a solar crop dryer as a protected drying system using solar thermal energy and/or solar PV-powered air circulation/control, with an optional hybrid backup, for controlled drying of agricultural and horticultural produce. The minimum technical specifications require an indirect solar crop dryer with forced convection. The systems are expected to handle fruits, vegetables, spices, medicinal and aromatic plants, grains and other agricultural or horticultural products. The dryers will have to use SS 304 food-grade trays and food-contact surfaces, while the drying temperature range is specified at 40°C to 70°C. Air circulation is to be achieved through solar-powered DC fans or blowers, with protection against bird and animal intrusion. bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 24, 2026 9:48 PM MP: Skill new currency and innovation new economy, says CM Mohan Yadav A day-long conclave on Samriddh Madhya Pradesh – 2047 was held in Bhopal today. Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav highlighted the importance of skills, research and innovation for the development of the state. During the conclave, 13 MoUs were also signed with various institutions to promote education, research, skill development and innovation. Speaking at the conclave, Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav said that skill is the new currency and innovation is the new economy. He said that central institutions in the state should work together in skill development, research and innovation, so that their benefits reach common people. The Chief Minister said that under the idea of One Institute-One Promise, every institution should set a development goal for the state and work to achieve it. This will create more opportunities and jobs for the youth.

The administrative approval was granted after the project received technical clearance from the competent authority, with the buildings expected to strengthen the state's examination infrastructure. According to Bihar Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh, the four-storey buildings will be constructed by the Building Construction Department. Land measuring between 1 acre and 1.5 acres has already been identified for each examination building. The project is aimed at creating dedicated examination facilities so that competitive and other examinations no longer have to rely extensively on school and college premises. Bihar examination buildings to accommodate 4,000 candidates Each examination building will be equipped to accommodate up to 4,000 candidates at a time. Examinations will be conducted under CCTV surveillance, while the facilities will also be used for storing answer sheets after examinations. The buildings can subsequently serve as evaluation centres for checking answer scripts. The facilities will include dedicated strong rooms for storing confidential examination material. Depending on requirements, answer sheets can also be barcoded and scanned at these centres. The infrastructure is therefore designed to support several stages of the examination process, from conducting tests to storing and evaluating answer sheets. The proposed buildings will also have fire alarms, firefighting equipment and disaster-management arrangements. CCTV cameras will operate around the clock, with continuous monitoring and recording to improve security at the examination centres. national_raw_news.title: India, Nepal discuss measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries 17 mins ago 12
national_raw_news.content: India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters. The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure. The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.
